# Decouple the storyline doc-drift guard from engine-owned heading text

**Headline:** `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` AC5b pins literal Markdown headings of the engine-owned reference `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (a git submodule that dev builds advance to the engine's latest dev tip), so any engine-side heading rename silently reddens this game's unit suite. Replace the heading pins with semantic anchors (API symbols, link resolution) plus a rename-tolerant section-structure check, and document why headings are not a cross-repo contract.

discovered-from: MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L

## Problem statement

Dev builds (`npm run build` → `engine:sync`) compose the **latest** engine dev tip via `git submodule update --remote core`, not the pinned release SHA. When core (dev tip `01d6bcc1`) renamed `## Engine adapter` → `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` in `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, the game's doc-drift guard (AC5b) reddened on **every** dev build, for **every** game repo that pins those headings — even though nothing in Main Street changed. The inline fix (commit `9f2c6185`) asserted the new heading, but the underlying coupling remains: a heading is an implementation detail of the engine's prose, not a contract the game depends on.

## Users / user stories

- As a **Main Street developer**, when I bump or dev-sync the engine, I want `npm test` to fail only for genuine breakage, so a green suite is trustworthy and a red suite means something real.
- As a **release engineer**, I want the doc guard to still fail loudly if the engine reference the game's adapters link to disappears or stops documenting the seam API, so releases cannot silently ship against vanished docs.
- As the **producer/operator**, I want the cross-repo doc dependency to be explicit and cheap to maintain, so a rename is a no-op (or a documented one-line change), not a cross-repo firefight.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No literal engine heading pins.** The AC5b block in `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` no longer asserts literal section-heading text of `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`; instead it asserts the semantic anchors the game genuinely depends on: the core reference exists, documents `createStorylineSystem` and the `@story-line` package, and names the `GymStorylineScene` consumer (any of these removed → guard fails).
- **AC2 — Rename tolerance is proven by a fixture test.** A new unit test in the same file feeds a fixture copy of the core doc with section headings renamed (e.g. `## Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author)` → `## Renamed seam section`) and asserts the contract check still passes; a negative fixture (missing `createStorylineSystem`) asserts the check still fails. *Metric: run the two fixture cases — tolerance passes, regression fails.*
- **AC3 — Link resolution preserved.** The guard keeps asserting that `docs/game/storylines.md` links to `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and that the target resolves on disk, and that the core reference is linked from `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `core/docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md`.
- **AC4 — Failure messages and rationale.** Any guard failure names the offending file and the missing anchor, and the test header comment explains that engine doc headings are not a cross-repo contract (with a pointer to this work item); a corresponding one-line note is added near the "thin adapters" paragraph of `docs/game/storylines.md` and in `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (Tests section) so the next engineer does not re-pin headings.
- **AC5 — Engine-revision tolerant and suite green.** The changed test scope passes with the submodule at the pinned SHA and with the engine dev tip the build composes; the full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- Game-side change only — do **not** edit files inside `core/` (engine-owned submodule, re-scaffolded by the game-repo scaffold); if an engine-side fix is later chosen, it is an engine-repo (CG) work item.
- Do not weaken the guard into a no-op: negative cases (missing file, missing symbol, broken link) must still fail the suite.
- No new dependencies; keep the guard in plain vitest + `node:fs`, consistent with the file's existing style.
- Do not change `configs/engine-pin.json` or the `core` gitlink as part of this work (they already agree at dev HEAD: pin `9ee194e009f5fade0bbbc141c03087d88bf373ef` == gitlink `9ee194e0`).

## Existing state

- Guard: `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, AC5b block asserts `['## API', '## Authoring seams', '## UI adapter', '## Gym demo']` against `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md` (created by MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY / MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR; heading pin baked in by commit `9f2c6185`).
- Engine doc at current pin (`9ee194e0`) has sections: API, Validation, Authoring seams (content, manifest, validator, author), UI adapter, Gym demo, Testing.
- The engine repo currently has **no** docs-consistency test and **no** heading anchor manifest (verified: no engine tests reference `docs/core-engine`, no anchor file) — so "engine owns the contract" would be net-new engine work.
- Sibling churn pattern already fixed inline: MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (pin/pointer mismatch when dev sync advances the submodule during a build).

## Desired change

1. Refactor the AC5b assertions into a small pure helper `checkCoreReferenceContract(coreDoc: string, headers: {file: string; link: boolean}): string[]` (returns missing anchors), so the same logic runs against the real file and against fixtures.
2. Replace the `['## API', …]` heading pins with: file-exists + `createStorylineSystem`/`@story-line`/`GymStorylineScene` presence + a structural check that the doc "documents the section topics" without pinning exact heading text (e.g. each required topic keyword found somewhere in the doc, tolerant of heading renames).
3. Add fixture-driven tests for rename tolerance (pass) and missing-symbol regression (fail).
4. Update the test header comment + the two doc notes (AC4).

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — AC5b block rewrite, tolerance/regression fixture tests, header rationale.
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/storyline-core-doc-renamed-heading.md` (new) — fixture mirroring the current core doc with headings renamed; or an inline string fixture to avoid duplicating a 400-line doc. Prefer the smallest fixture that provably exercises the renames; if inline, note that it must be refreshed on engine doc content changes.
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — one-line note that the guard asserts semantic anchors, not engine heading text.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — one-line note under "Tests" about the engine-doc heading non-contract.
- `core/docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `configs/engine-pin.json`, `core` gitlink — read-only references; must not be edited here.

## Related work

- MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR — created AC5b ("Storyline docs and drift guards", completed).
- MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY — canonical docs + doc-drift guard (completed).
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — browser-wait soak child where this was discovered (completed).
- MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F — sibling pin/pointer churn from dev-sync submodule advance (completed) — same root-cause class.
- MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV — open sibling that makes the composed engine explicit and fails when worktree `./core` lags the pin (complementary: this item makes the guard tolerant of the composed engine's docs).
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED — origin of dev-sync-on-build policy (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** the more thorough option — "the cross-repo doc contract should be owned by the engine (stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest)" — is deliberately **out of scope** here: it is net-new engine (CG) work affecting every game repo, and it is a producer decision. It is recorded as an open question in the Appendix; if approved, file a separate CG work item. This item stays game-side and is a prerequisite/valid regardless of that decision.
- **Assumption:** semantic symbols (`createStorylineSystem`, `@story-line`, `GymStorylineScene`) are stable markers of the seam API the game links to; the tolerance fixture must keep the renamed headings under the current section topics so it stays representative.
- **Risk — over-loosening:** a rename-tolerant check can drift into a no-op. Mitigated by AC2's negative fixture and AC3's link-resolution assertions.
- **Assumption:** dev builds keep composing the engine dev tip (policy from MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED); the guard must therefore tolerate any dev-tip doc revision.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (2026-10-25): "Should the cross-repo doc contract be owned by the engine (e.g. a stable heading contract / exported anchor manifest), rather than pinned by game tests?" — **OPEN QUESTION** — routed to producer for decision; **Recommended:** keep this item game-side (semantic anchors + rename tolerance), and file the engine-owned-contract option as a separate engine-repo (CG) work item only if the producer opts in — rationale: a heading is an implementation detail of engine prose, not a contract; semantic API symbols plus link resolution cover what games genuinely depend on, and any engine-side contract is net-new engine work hitting every game repo. Source: work-item description ("Follow-up worth deciding…"), research: engine repo has no docs-consistency test and no anchor manifest today; game repo cannot edit `core/`.
- Q2 (2026-10-25): "Should this item also fix the pin/pointer churn class (dev-sync advancing the submodule during builds)?" — Answer (triage): No — that is MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F (already fixed inline) / MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV (open); linked as related work above. Source: work-item + worklog search.

## Review log

- Finished completeness review: problem statement, ACs, constraints and key files added; no changes needed after first pass beyond adding the fixture strategy note.
- Finished capture-fidelity review: no user answers given (seed context + repo research only); Q1 recorded as OPEN QUESTION with recommendation.
- Finished related-work review: linked MS-0MVFMA9EW001MIQR, MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY, MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L, MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F, MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV, MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED; find-related report appended automatically.
- Finished risks & assumptions review: over-loosening mitigated by negative fixtures; engine-contract option isolated as scope-creep item.
- Finished polish & handoff: tightened wording; headline finalised.

## Related work (automated report from find-related)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F** – dev HEAD pin/pointer mismatch: engine-pin.json 01d6bcc1 vs core gitlink d907af9f (completed)
- **MS-0MVO26G5H0054SNV** – Worktree core submodule checkouts lag the pin, so test runs compose a stale engine (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: adapter, asserts, author, authoring, broke, browser, build, child, composes, contract, core, cross, delivery, dev, discovered, doc, docs, drift, engine, every, exported, follow, game, handled, heading, inline, latest, line, main, manifest, new, now, npm, old, owned, pin, pinned, pins, pointer, ran, rather, record, red, rename, repo, run, seam, seams, section, should, silently, since, stable, story, storylines, street, submodule, suite, sync, test, tests, tip, unit, validator, wait, whether, worth
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: adapter, author, authoring, browser, build, child, composes, contract, core, cross, dev, discovered, doc, docs, drift, engine, every, follow, game, handled, latest, line, main, manifest, new, now, npm, old, owned, pin, pins, ran, rather, record, red, repo, run, seam, seams, section, should, silently, stable, story, storylines, street, submodule, suite, sync, test, tests, unit, validator, wait, whether, worth
- `docs/game/storylines.md` — matched: adapter, author, authoring, browser, build, composes, contract, core, dev, doc, docs, drift, engine, every, exported, game, line, main, manifest, new, now, npm, old, pin, pinned, ran, rather, record, red, repo, run, seam, section, should, silently, stable, story, storylines, street, sync, test, tests, unit, validator, wait, whether, worth

# AI cost-aware event-choice tests

**Headline:** Failing-first unit tests pinning the cost-aware, presented-list-only AI event-choice contract for Main Street.

Part of **MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY** (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Goal

Encode the target contract for `decideEventChoice` before the policy change, so the implementation item is driven red → green. Tests use the existing programmatic option seam (`registerStorylineOptions`) because CSV `options` encoding cannot yet express `cost`/`extraEffect`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `cost-aware scoring` describe block in `tests/main-street/MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts` asserts `decideEventChoice` only ever returns an index into the **presented** option list: a cost-gated option that the draw-time filter drops is never selected, even when its successor chain would otherwise win.
- A test proves the pending-choice path uses the frozen draw-time snapshot (`getPendingStorylineOptions`): options registered *after* the pending choice was created do not change the AI's choice, and the returned index is valid for the frozen list.
- **Unit coverage.** Tests cover a cost-gated option being avoided (presented-list filter) and an extra-effect option that is only worthwhile once its delta is accounted for: the `extraEffect` option **is** chosen when its delta is counted, plus a control case with the same chain severities where the other option wins — so a no-delta implementation cannot pass both.
- A test proves `cost.coins` and `cost.reputation` are deducted from projected value using the same reputation weight as `eventSeverity` (`REPUTATION_SEVERITY_SCALE`), so an expensive-but-safe chain loses to a cheap-but-costly chain exactly at the modelled break-even.
- A test proves the policy is RNG-free: repeated calls return the same index and `state.rng` is never invoked (spy), so seeded replays stay byte-identical.
- The suite fails against today's `decideEventChoice` (state-unaware `getStorylineOptions`, no cost/extra-effect projection) — the red baseline is recorded in the item's completion comment.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts` with the new describe block and a small helper that registers a cost-bearing option list and resets the registry in `afterEach`.
- Reuse the existing synthetic chain-template CSV fixture for successor severity; add only the templates the new cases need.
- No production code changes in this item — the tests define the target contract and go green in sibling item **MS-0MVNU5EEC006ZCTF**.

## Key Files:

- `tests/main-street/MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts` — new cost-aware case block
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — subject under test (`decideEventChoice`, `optionChainSeverity`)
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `registerStorylineOptions` / `getPendingStorylineOptions` seams used by the fixtures
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StorylineOption` (`cost`, `extraEffect` from core)

## Verification

- `npm run build` clean; the new tests run through the project test skill (`/skill:test` changed scope) and are expected red until **MS-0MVNU5EEC006ZCTF** (Cost-aware AI event-choice policy) lands.

## Notes

- Test-first item: it exists so the contract is reviewable before implementation. It is committed together with the implementation in the same `dev` push (a red tree is never pushed).

# Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).
- `core/package.json` lines 31–32 declare the same two scripts **validly** (core has `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` (lines ~274–312) inherits all core scripts, then overrides repo entry points; `scaffold:game(s)` pass through unchanged.
- 9 sibling game repos (`../tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-f5-verify`, `tce-fresh-verify`, `tce-repos-f9`) carry the same two broken lines — separate repositories, out of scope for this item's ACs (see Follow-ups).
- Related inherited-scripts bug of the same class: 8 more core-only entries arrive broken in every game repo (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — the last breaks `npm run package`/`package:win|linux|mac`). Excluded from scope (see Follow-ups).

## Desired change

1. Remove `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from this repo's root `package.json` (hand edit; see Constraints).
2. In `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, filter the core-only keys out of the inherited scripts map — a small explicitly-named drop-list (or drop any inherited script that still references the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target) with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Add/extend unit tests on both sides; bump the `./core` submodule pointer to the engine commit carrying the template fix.
4. Update `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (and the one-line core-doc clarification in Tableau-Card-Engine).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — remove the two `scaffold:game(s)` entries (this repo).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson`: drop core-only inherited scripts (template fix, engine repo).
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — extend MANIFEST fixture with `scaffold:game(s)` and assert they are omitted from the rendered `package.json`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` (new) — regression guard: no `scaffold:game(s)` declared; every `scaffold*` script target exists.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo entry point; note `scaffold:game(s)` are core-only.
- `.gitmodules` / `gitlink core` — submodule pointer bump to the engine commit with the template fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Dead-key approach is undocumented assumption.** Assumption (recorded, not operator-confirmed): the fix is the narrow one from the item title — drop only `scaffold:game(s)`; the other 8 broken inherited scripts are a separate discovered follow-up (below). If the operator prefers the general filter (fixes all 10), AC1–AC5 grow; flagged, not blocking.
- **R2 — Submodule bump pulls unrelated engine commits.** The engine `dev` head is ahead of the pinned submodule (pinned `9ee194e0…` vs engine `dev` `1c9900a1…`). Mitigation: keep the bump to a reviewable commit; full suite must stay green (AC5).
- **R3 — Incomplete inheritance semantics.** Filtering only `scaffold:game(s)` is a stop-gap while the general class remains broken; over time more core-only scripts may be added. Mitigation: follow-up item tracks the general fix (`discovered-from` link).
- **R4 — Re-scaffold destructiveness discovered during intake.** If the template's preserve-on-re-scaffold behaviour is later expected to keep repo-local scripts, that is a separate enhancement — out of scope here.
- **Scope-creep guard:** sibling-repo clean-up, the 8-script general fix, and template local-script preservation are all recorded as follow-ups, not folded into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — "[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts" (the `discovered-from` parent; same scaffold-template class of bug).
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED ↔ CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — engine-sync wiring precedent: core template change (in engine repo) + game-repo side + re-scaffold; the MS↔CG pairing model this item follows.
- **CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R** — version policy in `renderPackageJson` (the same function being changed).
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** — sibling-repo port of a core template guard; same cross-repo pattern.
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** — scaffold vite.config template ownership.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** – [test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)
- **MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O** – Engine dev tip renamed the story-line docs seam section (game doc-drift test pinned old heading) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, ac4, appear, banner, broken (+68 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: appear, banner, changes, context, core (+54 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, appear (+50 more)
> Assessment: `MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL` and `MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED` are genuinely related (same template/entry-point class). `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` matched on keyword noise (story-line docs seam) and is **not** relevant to this item; repo-file matches are incidental IDF matches. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0.md`.

## Follow-ups (recorded; out of scope)

- **Generalise the inherited-scripts filter** to all core-only entries that reference the absent game-repo `scripts/` tree (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — `build:electron-main` breakage disables `npm run package*` in every game repo). `discovered-from: MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`.
- **Re-scaffold sibling game repos** (golf, blackjack, lost-cities, coloretto, feudalism, beleaguered-castle, f5/fresh-verify, repos-f9) or hand-remove the two lines; each is its own repo/worklog item.
- **Template preservation of repo-local scripts** on re-scaffold (R4).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview was required: the seed context and acceptance criteria were sufficiently defined, and repository search resolved the description's open question ("resolve which is true first") directly:

- Q: Does `renderPackageJson` emit the two broken scripts, or were they hand-copied into game repos? — Answer (agent, repo search): It emits them **by inheritance** — `renderPackageJson` copies the core manifest's whole `scripts` map; `core/package.json` lines 31–32 are the source, and the rendered fixture (core test + node simulation) reproduces both keys.
